title: Press Edition — Cream Linen Masthead
description: A wide letterbox newsletter hero modeled after the restrained authority of Stripe Press and Every — cream paper-texture ground, a floating mustard issue badge, and a monospaced read-time pill anchor a single bold teaser line.
philosophy: This template believes a newsletter header should feel like the front page of a small literary journal, not a promotional email. It rejects bright gradients, decorative icons, and brand-color maximalism in favor of careful typographic hierarchy and tactile paper noise. It exists for independent writers and editorial brands whose readers open every issue because the design itself signals seriousness. The room is a subscriber's inbox, not a sales funnel.
goodFor: Weekly newsletter edition announcements with a single punchy topic line
Independent publishing brands seeking a print-editorial email identity
Substack or Every-style digest headers dropped into email campaigns
Issue-numbered series where the badge and read-time chip are key UI signals
avoidFor: Product launches requiring full-bleed photography or high-contrast CTAs
Multi-panel chart or data-heavy quarterly review slides
Fast-paced social story formats needing kinetic energy and bold color blocks
Conference or event promotions where urgency and visual noise drive clicks
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like the front page of a small literary journal arriving in the mail — cream linen texture underfoot, restrained and unhurried. Compositional rhythm is airy: a single commanding teaser line holds the center while a warm accent badge and a quiet monospaced chip provide the only points of visual punctuation. Avoid gradient washes, decorative illustration, or anything that reads as promotional; the mood is quiet editorial authority, the kind of design that signals seriousness before a single word is read.

examples.layoutNotes: Wide letterbox canvas with a 7% horizontal outer margin and a slim top band reserved for the masthead rule line and publication wordmark. An issue badge floats upper-left, pinned to the masthead baseline, while the single teaser headline sits centered in a column spanning roughly two-thirds of the total width, vertically biased toward the upper half with generous breathing room beneath. A read-time pill anchors the lower-left corner, keeping the bottom edge active without competing with the headline. No header band or decorative frame — the paper texture ground and typographic hierarchy carry the full structural load.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the interior opening spread of a small curated literary digest — restrained, deliberate, and quietly self-assured, as if the design itself is the credential. A cream linen ground with subtle paper noise lends tactility; asymmetric left-weighted composition lets the eye travel without urgency or sales pressure. A single editorial pull quote or tight teaser paragraph commands the dominant zone, its gravity offset by a sparse monospaced metadata chip on the right. Avoid decorative icons, gradient washes, and promotional crowding — the unoccupied surface is structural, not accidental.

examples.layoutNotes: Wide letterbox canvas on a 12-column grid with an 8% outer margin on each side; primary content — a pull quote, short teaser paragraph, or terse feature list — occupies columns 2–8, left-aligned with generous top breathing space. A thin horizontal rule beneath a small monospaced section label (e.g., 'In this issue' or 'From the editor') supplies hierarchy through weight contrast and line work rather than size jumps. A read-time pill or issue-number badge floats right in columns 10–11, vertically centered against the text block. An edition marker or folio sits flush to the bottom-right baseline, completing the masthead grammar.
